text:
maya_dev: kicking off canary for Oxbridge-15B int4 on dedicated-canary pool. noticing mem fragmentation during ramp and a small quality dip on summarization eval (ROUGE-L -1.8). logs show repeated KV eviction (~every 12s) and OOM spikes when microbatching >4. deploying with default route config for now.

owen_ml: which quant pipeline? PTQ or QK+GP? can you paste route config + perf numbers? :eyes:

maya_dev: PTQ with per-column clamp, using model artifact oxbridge-15b-int4-v1. Route snippet:
```
route: /v1/models/oxbridge-15b/versions/int4
batching:
  microbatch_size: 8
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  max_new_tokens: 256
  slot_reserve: 0.06
```
Perf baseline on staging (small load): p50 88ms p95 420ms cost ~0.62 tok
Under load (steady ramp) we get p95 760ms and KV evict logs: "kv_cache trimmed 512MB"

li_engineer: microbatch_size 8 is probably the issue with our prefetch profile. Try microbatch 2-4 and increase slot_reserve to 0.12. Also try lowering max_new_tokens default to 128 for canary — reduces KV growth.

sarah_research: quality dip might be quantization fallout on long context summaries. What's prompt length distribution for that eval? Could be head token sensitivity.

maya_dev: eval prompt stats: median context 1200 tokens, tail 3800 tokens. Summaries typically 180-300 new tokens.

owen_ml: ok try this quick plan:
- deploy canary with microbatch_size: 3, slot_reserve: 0.12
- set max_new_tokens: 128 for the route
- enable KV prefetch warming for first-requests (warmup=3)
- compare ROUGE/ROUGE-L and p95

maya_dev: applying now, will post logs. also toggling eviction policy from 'aggressive' -> 'LRU-preserve-prefix'

deploy-bot: deploy started by @maya_dev — canary/oxbridge-int4 update -> in_progress

maya_dev: initial metrics after change: p50 95ms p95 480ms, KV trim events reduced by ~80%, OOM 0 for last 30m. Quality: ROUGE-L diff now -0.4 vs baseline (much better). Still some tail errors on 3800-context cases.

li_engineer: for tails we should enable generation-window warmup and increase evict_threshold for KVs for routes with >2k context. try: generation_window: 1024, kv_evict_threshold: 0.25

maya_dev: applied kv_evict_threshold 0.25 and gen window 1024. logs show fewer evictions but memory plateau higher — acceptable for canary. p95 500ms, ROUGE-L -0.2. Will run full eval set overnight.

sarah_research: if post-eval still shows small regressions, run a small fp16 A/B and compute token-level divergence to see where quantization mismatches concentrate.

owen_ml: agree. also add a flag to the canary to auto-fallback to oxbridge-15b-int8 if p95 > 800ms or rouge drop > 1.0.

ops-bot: note: created incident runbook link https://internal/runs/oxbridge-canary-1746002222

maya_dev: thanks all — overnight eval scheduled. will report final numbers tomorrow. :thumbsup:
